title: VS Code extension refuses to connect to a daemon whose /health reports another project
description:
Follow-up from task-e7f4026a (HIGH, a seat adopted another project's daemon through a stale daemon.json). That bug's description asks to check "the IDE plugins' daemon adoption". Its DoD covers JetBrains only (task-90664db1), so this row is the VS Code parity. It lands in BACKLOG for the human to schedule.

The gap, checked by the planning architect on 2026-10-30, is wider than in JetBrains. moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts ensureDaemonRunning() and waitForDaemonInfo():
- compare only the projectPath written in .moe/daemon.json (pathsMatch);
- then trust isPortOpen(host, port), with no PID check at all.
So once this project's daemon dies and another project's daemon takes the recorded port, connect() opens ws://<host>:<port>/ws to the other project's board.

Deliverable:
- Before connect() opens /ws, probe http://<host>:<port>/health with a bounded timeout and a body capped at 64 KiB. Compare its projectPath by the comparable-path rule of packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts comparableProjectPath (D:\x == D:/x == /mnt/d/x).
- On a foreign reply:
  - open no client;
  - treat daemon.json as stale, deleting it only while it still names the pid, port and startedAt that were read;
  - log and show which project that daemon serves;
  - start this project's daemon, which takes the next free port.
- An unknown reply (unreachable, non-JSON, oversize, no projectPath) keeps today's behavior.
- Mirror the decisions landed by the JetBrains fix (task-90664db1): read its code and handoff memory first.
- Tests in moe-vscode/tests. The vm harnesses transpile single files with a closed require shim (mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness), so check which harnesses load MoeDaemonClient.ts before adding an import to it.

Ordering: MoeDaemonClient.ts is in CQ-RF06's and CQ-RF06b's plans (task-98ffe33f, task-032c9739). This row dependsOn both, plus the JetBrains fix.

Not in scope: the proxy, the wrappers, the JetBrains plugin, the daemon.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0): cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile
definitionOfDone: A daemon at the port .moe/daemon.json names, whose /health projectPath is another project, gets no /ws client from the extension. The stale daemon.json is removed only while it still names the pid, port and startedAt that were read, and this project's daemon is started. Proven by a moe-vscode test.
This project's path in any spelling (D:\x, D:/x, /mnt/d/x) counts as the same project. Unreachable, non-JSON, oversize and projectPath-less /health replies keep today's behavior. Proven by test rows.
`cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile` exits 0, with its output supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.note: Read full task comment and landed dependency evidence (RF06, RF06b, JetBrains, corrected path contract), archived JetBrains handoff and proxy/IDE sources. Added 34 tests incl corrected POSIX-case/UNC/WSL contract, real HTTP deadline/socket cleanup, guarded deletion and real /ws integration. RED: node --test tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs exits 1; D foreign/configured/second-foreign/replaced each assertion-fail because baseline opens 1 forbidden /ws. Helper rows await new exports. Existing shared dirty paths (scripts/docs/board etc.) untouched. No local relative runtime imports will be added; existing closed vm shims require lazy node:http/node:url loading inside probe.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts. Use node builtins only, with no new local import.

1. Path rule.
- Export comparableProjectPath, mirroring packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:
  - a drive path goes through path.win32.normalize, then '/' separators, no trailing slash, lowercase;
  - /mnt/<d> maps to <d>: after normalizing. Use path.posix.normalize of the raw string on win32, and path.resolve elsewhere.
- If RF06 already landed an identical rule, reuse it instead of adding a second one.
- pathsMatch delegates to it. Its three existing call sites then accept every spelling of this project: the daemon.json checks in getDaemonInfo and ensureDaemonRunning, and the STATE_SNAPSHOT rootPath check. That also stops a Windows daemon from being deleted and duplicated by a Remote-WSL window.
- Export isAbsoluteAnyOs (drive, UNC or POSIX), mirroring the proxy.

2. Probe. Export probeDaemonIdentity(host, port, projectPath, {timeoutMs = 1500}). It returns {kind:'same'}, {kind:'foreign', projectPath} or {kind:'unknown'}.
- Make one node:http GET of /health.
- Use one overall timer plus the request timeout.
- Count body bytes and stop at 64 KiB.
- Settle once, through a done guard.
- Clear the timer and destroy the socket on every path.
- Never reject.

3. Export removeDaemonJsonIfUnchanged(file, {pid, port, startedAt}).
- Re-read the file through readDaemonJsonText and unlink it only when all three fields still match.
- Log, and never throw, on any error.

4. getDaemonInfo also returns pid, startedAt and a fromConfig flag, keeping host and port as today. Check every caller still compiles.

5. connect(): probe after getDaemonInfo and before setConnectionState('connecting') and new WebSocket.
- Foreign, from daemon.json:
  - log the event;
  - show a warning: 'Moe: the daemon on <host>:<port> serves <served>, not this workspace (<project>). Starting this project's daemon on the next free port.';
  - call removeDaemonJsonIfUnchanged;
  - await startDaemon('start', projectPath);
  - re-read getDaemonInfo once and probe once more. A second foreign or missing answer throws, so the callers' existing error and reconnect handling applies. Never loop.
- Foreign, from a configured moe.daemon.port: show an error naming both projects and throw. Delete nothing and start nothing.
- Unknown or same: proceed exactly as today.

Error handling:
- The probe never throws.
- A refusal opens no WebSocket and leaves no ping interval.
- connectInProgress is still reset in finally.
- The STATE_SNAPSHOT mismatch check stays as the second line of defense.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented the corrected proxy path contract, absolute-path classifier, capped 1.5s overall/request deadline probe with socket cleanup, nonthrowing guarded deletion, metadata provenance and pre-/ws recovery/configured-port refusal. Lazy typed builtin requires avoid changing closed vm harness imports. One bounded respawn/reprobe, unknown preserves legacy. Inspection found recovery's getDaemonInfo reread could delete a concurrent foreign-project replacement after guarded removal kept it (JetBrains gotcha); added red regression and read-only retry getDaemonInfo(false). Added successful recovery/concurrent connect test. Fresh narrow run: 35 pass/0 fail (initial replacement repro 1 assertion-fail). No changes outside the two planned files.

comments.author: architect-bd1eb82d
comments.content:
Architect note (architect-bd1eb82d, 2026-10-30): this row now also dependsOn task-25ba449a, which corrects the path rule it mirrors.

Step-2 item 1 describes the OLD moe-proxy comparableProjectPath: path.win32.normalize for drive paths, posix-normalize of the raw /mnt string on win32, and path.resolve otherwise. On Windows that rule sends an absolute POSIX path through path.resolve, so /home/qa/OtherProject and /home/qa/otherproject both become c:/home/qa/otherproject. That is a false "same" for a WSL daemon.

task-25ba449a replaces it with one OS-independent contract for absolute paths, documented on comparableProjectPath in packages/moe-proxy/src/utils.ts:
- Drive and UNC forms: \ and / both separate, segments are collapsed, and case is folded.
- \\wsl$\<distro>\x and \\wsl.localhost\<distro>\x name the distro's POSIX /x.
- POSIX paths keep their case on every OS, and /mnt/<d> maps to d:.
- Only a relative path is first resolved natively.

When implementing here, port the landed contract from utils.ts, not the algorithm text in step 2. Add the contract rows to section A: POSIX case on win32, \\srv\share\p equal to //SRV/SHARE/P/, and a WSL share equal to its POSIX path. The rest of the plan is unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Relying on the existing STATE_SNAPSHOT rootPath check alone: rejected.
  - It already disconnects on a mismatch and deletes daemon.json.
  - But by then a /ws client is open on the foreign board, which DoD 1 forbids.
  - Its unconditional unlink is also a TOCTOU.
- A separate daemonIdentity.ts module: rejected. The vm harnesses transpile MoeDaemonClient.ts alone with a closed require shim, and five of them load it. The helpers are exported from MoeDaemonClient.ts, as RF06 did.
- Probing only in ensureDaemonRunning: rejected. connect() also serves a configured moe.daemon.port and every reconnect, so the probe sits where the socket opens.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- VS Code adopts the port from daemon.json after a pathsMatch on the file's projectPath plus isPortOpen. It has no PID check.
- pathsMatch does path.resolve plus lowercase on win32, without /mnt folding. A Remote-WSL window can therefore misjudge a Windows daemon as stale, delete its daemon.json and start a duplicate.
- On 'open' the client only sends GET_STATE and pings. The STATE_SNAPSHOT handler compares payload.project.rootPath, then disconnects and unlinks.
- tests/daemon-start.test.cjs shows how to build a MoeDaemonClient in the vm with stubbed vscode and child_process.
- isEpicFinal on this row is only the order fallback of a grab-bag epic with no designated finalTaskId. The regression scope is the full moe-vscode suite.
planningNotes.risks:
- RF06 and RF06b rewrite MoeDaemonClient.ts first. Read the landed bytes and reuse their path helper where it is the same rule.
- The connect-level tests need real servers in the test process. node --test runs async tests, so never spawnSync there.
- Closing the WebSocketServer, the http server and the client in every test avoids hanging the runner.
- Windows path.resolve differs, so run the suite on Windows node too.
